text:
maria (Support): heads-up — we started getting a spike of 429s from two enterprise customers after the rate-policy canary went live in eu-west-1 ~10m ago. They report errors during heavy batch ingestion jobs, lower retry rates than expected.

kevin (Platform): thanks Maria — can you paste an example error body + headers and a quick repro curl?

maria (Support): sure. here's a sanitized curl that hits the problematic path and the response we see repeatedly:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"bulk test"}'
```

Response snippet: 
```json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after_seconds": 120,
  "quota": {"limit": 6000, "remaining": 0}
}
```

And headers: x-rate-limit-limit: 6000, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-canary-policy: rollout-v2

josh (SRE): ok that's interesting — rollout-v2 was supposed to be gentle in eu. Maria, can you share client timestamps or the batch size the customer used? want to check burst vs sustained.

maria (Support): they ran 12 requests/s sustained for ~15m during an ingestion window; usually they were at ~4r/s. They switched on a single-threaded parallel runner.

kevin (Platform): @deploy-bot — what percentage of traffic was the canary config affecting in eu-west-1?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout "rate-policy/rollout-v2" active in eu-west-1; weight=8%; started=1914500000; evaluation windows open.

kevin (Platform): weight 8% + prefix caching disabled for these endpoints could push some clients over thresholds during bursts. Our intended behavior was to shape to per-customer burst buckets, but looks like the mapping rule missed higher-tier customers.

lia (Product): was this a config change to per-tenant burst budget or a global cap? Need to know if enterprise tiers lost headroom.

kevin (Platform): rollout-v2 moved from global token-based limit -> hybrid tenant-aware buckets. There was an edge-case where tenants with legacy quota-metadata weren't mapped and fell back to default (lower) burst. That's our likely cause.

sophia (Eng-Oncall): given live 429s from paying customers, recommend pausing the canary immediately and rollback to rollout-v1. I can run the rollback.

josh (SRE): agree. we should also open temporary relaxation rules for affected tenant ids to avoid immediate customer impact while rollback completes. Maria — do you have the tenant ids?

maria (Support): yes, I have tenant: acme-inc and tenant: bluebridge — both hit the limit at 2023-07-25T14:02:xxZ and again at 14:07.

kevin (Platform): ok., steps: 1) pause canary (stop traffic weighting), 2) apply tenant-level override (increase burst by 3x) for acme-inc & bluebridge, 3) monitor 5-10m and confirm error rate drop, 4) rollback config to rollout-v1 if stable.

sophia (Eng-Oncall): executing step 1 now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout "rate-policy/rollout-v2" paused by sophia; new weight=0% at 1914501390.

sophia (Eng-Oncall): step 2 applied tenant overrides. CLI: `rwctl quotas override --tenant acme-inc --burst 18000 --expires 15m` and same for bluebridge.

maria (Support): they report immediate improvement on first retry for a few requests. Still seeing sporadic 429s but much reduced. :thumbsup:

josh (SRE): I'm rolling a temporary smoothing rule at the edge to add jittered retry guidance and increase allowed short-window bursts for those tenancy headers.

kevin (Platform): tracking action items for postmortem: 1) audit mapping logic for legacy quota-metadata, 2) add a canary test that includes a simulated enterprise burst profile, 3) add alerting for tenant-level 429 spike (automated) so support can be alerted earlier.

lia (Product): add product-level follow-up to rethink default fallback behavior — should never drop enterprise tier to default low burst.

maria (Support): do we need to proactively reach out to acme-inc & bluebridge? they're on high-touch plans.

kevin (Platform): yes — I'll patch eng-cs with a short blurb to send and cc ops; include timeline and that we've paused rollout and applied temporary overrides.

deploy-bot: rate-policy rollback to rollout-v1 scheduled by kevin at 1914501600; rolling status=initiated.

sophia (Eng-Oncall): monitoring logs: 429 rate for affected tenants down from 65/min -> 4/min over last 7m. Looks stable.

lia (Product): good catch everyone. please assign owners for the audit and canary-test items. I'll take product owner for default fallback behavior.

kevin (Platform): I'll own the mapping logic audit and add unit/integration tests. josh please take the edge smoothing/alerting work.

josh (SRE): on it. I'll draft an alert runbook too.

maria (Support): I'll notify both customers and share the rollback + ETA.

kevin (Platform): final note: before we resume rollout-v2, we need a synthetic that runs a 10-15m sustained 12r/s burst per tenant to verify no regressions. Add to the canary gate.

lia (Product): agreed. we'll gate on that and on a 0.1% SLA degradation check for 30m window.

maria (Support): closing loop with customers now. thanks team.

sophia (Eng-Oncall): marking thread resolved for now; reopening if 429s spike again. :white_check_mark:
